title: autotune: default batching/caching + quantization profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Reduce per-token unit costs across hosted and dedicated deployments by providing safe defaults for batching and prefix/KV caching, adding per-model quantization profile recommendations, and exposing a small unit-economics CLI/tooling surface for operators. This PR bundles the autotune defaults, quant profiles, and the initial 'uecon' CLI used by runbooks.

Summary of changes:
- Introduce AutotuneDefaults service that suggests batch_size, max_latency_slo, and cache TTLs per model family and workload fingerprint.
- Add quantization profile metadata for curated model variants (int8/4-bit recommendations + expected quality delta estimates).
- Implement UEcon CLI (internal) that computes per-request unit-econ using batch/caching/quant profiles and simulates cost/latency tradeoffs for proposed configs.
- Wire defaults into runtime: runtime consults AutotuneDefaults on model load and when route config is unset. Defaults are non-breaking and can be overridden per-route.
- Migration: add schema migrations for model_registry.quant_profiles and add config flags to opt out.

Testing & rollout plan:
- Unit tests for AutotuneDefaults scoring and quant profile parsing. Integration tests run against perf-canary with synthetic workloads to validate latency SLOs.
- Start canary rollout: 5% of traffic to models with defaults applied for 48h, metrics auto-compare (latency, p99, quality regression).
- If no regressions, promote to 100% over 24h. Manual rollback flags available.

Notes: This PR is intended to be low-risk: defaults are conservative and annotated. The UEcon CLI is intentionally read-only for hosted customers and requires RBAC to run in private deployments. Related Linear: ENG-1243, ENG-1299. Related support ticket: SUP-4281.
